# CLAIMs with `line` `dependence-and-domination`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Wholes, parts and dependence** — what wholes and their parts owe and can claim of each other, and when a dependence becomes domination or exploitation — control over the terms on which a dependence is met, not the size of the dependence, decides which way it runs and whether a whole's need of a part is the part's hold; exploitation and domination are judged against a standard declared with the judgment; and those who control an arrangement others depend on owe accountability and justification that rise with how indispensable it has become and how durably their choices narrow what is later open. "Organization" here is TERM-074's sense 1, a relational arrangement, unless an entry says otherwise, and the bearers of obligations, agents or roles, are kept apart from the ground of the obligation; split from organizational-normativity (ADR-100).

| [CLAIM-686](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-686.md) v2 | Where a dependent party's claims on an arrangement's controllers fail of legibility, volitional efficacy or correctability in the controlling organization, the dependent lacks effective means of influence and challenge, and where they fail so at every party able to constrain the controllers it lacks effective protection; justified withdrawal lies outside those three achievements, so the domination threshold's third condition is met by failures of normative efficacy only together with a failure of exit, and is not those failures restated | The assistant's, from the step-12 ideas of the filing of the exchange "Analyze technological civilization trap" (2026-11-13), offered as "the threshold in the record's own terms" and accepted by the owner on 2026-11-13 ("file the still unfiled stuff"). The idea was that [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s third condition, inadequate accountability, could be restated as the failure of [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md)'s legibility, volitional efficacy or correctability for the dependent party's claims, and that this held nearly by definition. Checked against both entries, it holds only in part. [CLAIM-523](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-523.md) states the three as needed, not as sufficient, so a failure of any one, for the dependent's claims, entails that the dependent lacks effective influence and challenge; the converse does not follow.
